title: Marriage
definition: Marriage is the covenant relationship established by God between one man and one woman for lifelong faithfulness, companionship, service, and witness.
summary: Marriage is God's covenant design for a lifelong relationship that reflects faithfulness, love, and spiritual growth.
christFocus: Jesus honored God's design for marriage and the marriage covenant points ultimately to Christ's faithful love for His Church.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Marriage is God's creation, not merely a human arrangement. From the beginning, God designed marriage as a covenant union between a man and a woman, marked by faithfulness, companionship, and shared life before Him.

Marriage is meant to reflect covenant love. It requires sacrifice, truth, forgiveness, patience, purity, service, and perseverance. Because sin affects every relationship, marriage also requires humility and grace.

In Scripture, marriage points beyond itself to the covenant faithfulness of Christ toward His Church. This gives marriage dignity and seriousness, while also reminding believers that Christ is the ultimate hope of every marriage.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people define marriage by emotion, convenience, or culture. This doctrine matters because it roots marriage in God's design and calls husbands and wives to covenant faithfulness rather than self-centeredness.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Honor marriage as God's covenant design. If married, pursue faithfulness, sacrificial love, forgiveness, and prayer. If unmarried, honor marriage by purity, wisdom, and encouragement toward those who are married.
